name: Bondada Engineering Limited
sector: Telecom and renewable EPC, O&M and power investments
summary: Rapid EPC scaling is evidenced, but supplier-financed cash conversion and a shift into leveraged asset ownership change the investment case. Completed conditional annual models show substantial funding dependence. Mainboard migration remains in-principle only; no numeric IAS or implementation recommendation.
identity_note: Primary sources identify legal company and listing; verify any later migration before execution.
score_note: Canonical historical quality arithmetic retained. Persistent CASH 2 caps GQS 5. IAS NS for genuine project-funding/ownership and implementation gaps, not unperformed annual calculations.

gates.reason: Current audit/controls positive; capital allocation and related EPC eliminations require monitoring, no severe abuse established.
Historical cash differences/ageing subtotal remain bounded; no fabricated clean bridge. Historical trend scoreable, forward project precision not.
Large modeled core/project needs exceed verified exact disbursement terms; not a finding of certain inability to fund.
Dated matching price/lot and 60 observed proxy rows; effective migration, BSE restrictions/depth not verified.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Bondada has demonstrated substantial EPC execution and revenue growth, but is not yet a proven self-financing renewable annuity compounder. FY26 consolidated revenue ₹2,842.81 crore and owners’ PAT ₹203.48 crore coexist with a large supplier-financing-supported working-capital expansion. The linked base case produces 17.76% annual price return from the dated secondary ₹290.60 close only if substantial new financing and assumed project economics materialize. It is not a supported expected return. Hold — unresolved project terms and cash-conversion confidence; distinguish this from an evidenced default or governance failure. [S1][S5][S6][S7][S95]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Bondada Engineering Limited, BSE 543971/BONDADA, ISIN INE0Q8P01029. BSE SME as of 20 October 2026: BSE 9 September and NSE 14 October in-principle migration approvals are not an effective mainboard commencement notice. FY26 is first Ind AS reporting, transition 1 April 2024, with restated FY25; older Indian GAAP is separately labeled. All model monetary amounts are ₹ crore unless per-share. Five-year synthetic annual horizon, 15% nominal hurdle and ₹5 lakh illustrative position. Historical filings are primary issuer reports hosted on public filing mirrors; dated price/history is secondary. Current capital 111,671,485 shares agrees with April allotment and official security master, lot 200. Remaining 78,000 options are included in model dilution. [S1][S2][S10][S95] [S91]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Strong growth earns REV 9, not an exceptional persistence score based on a single year. GOV6/MOAT5/DUR6/CAP6/CASH 2/BAL4/EXEC7/EARN8 distinguish execution strength from cash and funding risk. CAP uses a supplier-financing-inclusive historical proxy, not management ROCE or an assumed return on unfinished IPP assets. Persistent cash weakness caps GQS 5. Historical quality is scoreable with medium confidence; R remains NS because project disbursement/recourse/cost timing and modeled incremental funding are not verified. D3 reflects calculated severe capital loss and financing sensitivity, P4 reflects demanding concurrent operating/funding assumptions. L remains NS because secondary turnover proxies and security-master lot do not establish restrictions, spreads or market depth. No weights are renormalized. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S13][S95]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Incorporated 2012, the group supplies telecom and renewable EPC, O&M and manufactured infrastructure products. FY26 segment revenue is EPC ₹2,533.5791 crore, services ₹131.0562 crore and products ₹178.1697 crore, versus ₹1,343.1833/99.3898/128.3837 crore. O&M is recurring service exposure, not the majority of revenue. New Onix solar and TN/AP battery-storage BOO projects require owned assets, debt service and equity, unlike customer-funded EPC. Internal construction for a controlled project must be eliminated in consolidated revenue/profit rather than valued twice. The 6 October 270 MWp award includes tax, explicitly reports related/promoter-group interest and leaves the counterparty unnamed; it cannot automatically be equated to independent customer revenue or identified as the 225 MWAC Onix project solely from capacity similarity. [S1][S6][S8][S11][S12]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Execution references, procurement relationships and ability to qualify for institutional tenders are meaningful advantages, but competitive bidding limits pricing power. POC accounting depends on cost-to-complete and liquidated-damage estimates, not just megawatts announced. Backlog is concentrated even where recognized-year customer sales appear more diversified; those measures are not contradictory. Comparator fit: Sterling and Wilson is a larger international EPC/O&M specialist with different geographic/contract risk; KPI combines IPP ownership and CPP/EPC, useful for capital-intensity comparison but not a clean EPC margin benchmark; Waaree RTL’s proposed ASPL investment illustrates another changing EPC/manufacturing perimeter, not a completed comparable transaction. No current peer multiple has been verified, so exit multiples are explicit sensitivities rather than an invented sector average. Bondada’s telecom/manufacturing mix and emerging BESS ownership preclude a single annuity multiple across all sales. [S1][S13][S18][S19][S20]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Indian-GAAP FY23/FY24 revenue ₹370.5884/800.7223 crore; FY25 original ₹1,571.3768 crore, restated Ind AS ₹1,570.9568 crore; FY26 ₹2,842.805 crore. Three-year endpoint CAGR is 97.22%, not a five-year organic growth rate. FY26 growth 80.96% is chiefly EPC: segment addition ₹1,190.3958 crore, versus services ₹31.6664 and products ₹49.7860 crore. Older acquisitions and scope changes prevent declaring the entire multi-year CAGR organic. Group/owners’ PAT were FY23 ₹17.1307/16.7368, FY24 ₹46.3080/44.7273, FY25 original ₹115.3677/111.8823, FY25 restated ₹113.1713/109.6826 and FY26 ₹211.0791/203.4762 crore. Q1 FY27 reviewed group revenue ₹691.6547 versus ₹557.8292 crore, owners’ PAT ₹52.8944 versus ₹38.2591 crore. Standalone ₹47.6953 crore PAT is not group owners’ profit. TTM arithmetic gives revenue ₹2,976.6305 and owners’ PAT ₹218.1115 crore; no TTM CFO is invented. [S1][S3][S4][S9]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: July Onix 60% share purchase cost ₹0.006 crore is not the economic investment: its 225 MWAC portfolio requires major construction funding. Issuer cites 25-year MSEDCL PPA and estimated annual revenue ₹150.48 crore, not realized revenue. October sanction supplies ₹900 crore term debt plus ₹11.25 crore nonfund facility, not ₹911.25 crore spendable cash. TN BESS has Canara sanction and eligible ₹108 crore VGF, whose receipt timing is conditional; AP 450 MWh BOO announcement gives ₹627 crore broad contract consideration, not an audited capex budget. The model therefore labels AP ₹600 crore cost/₹420 crore debt/₹62 crore revenue as assumptions, not disclosures. A further 2 GW Andhra initiative and management’s ₹250 crore first-phase land/equity discussion are separated as a stress, not included as another ₹9,000 crore external EPC sale. Manufacturing ₹120–130 crore aspirations and KCS 75% partnership agreement represent future allocation/execution demands; defence customer references do not prove a mature earnings stream. [S5][S6][S7][S11][S12][S17]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: FY26 MD remuneration ₹1.2888 crore and CFO ₹0.6588 crore total ₹1.9476 crore, under 1% of group PAT. Disclosed prior promoter loans were repaid; related transactions are not by themselves misconduct. Review capital flows across subsidiaries because common funding can transmit project stress to the listed parent. Sreedar Mohan’s current audit/IFC and bank-return reporting are positive; KAMs specifically address contract progress/cost estimates and receivable ECL, not qualifications. Edit-log preservation wording is retained as qualified by software coverage, not blanket proof against manipulation. GST appeal ₹1.7578 crore with ₹0.1433 crore deposit is a contingent claim, not a final adverse outcome. BGs ₹516.1183 crore and capital commitments ₹12.3356 crore are separate from funded debt. Delivery test: May 2025 ₹2,600 crore FY26 revenue aspiration was exceeded; claimed 50–60% growth through 2030 is not yet achieved. April 2026 approximately 1.3 GWp cumulative commissioning and FY27 aspiration 1.5 GWp additional must be checked against October claimed 1.7 GWp cumulative, not described as full-year delivery. [S1][S5][S14][S16]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 core EBIT=PBT ₹284.6626+finance ₹40.7331−other income ₹8.2940=₹317.1017 crore,11.15% margin. FY25 restated core EBIT ₹164.1807 crore. FY26 CFO ₹124.5658 versus −₹140.9309 crore gives two-year CFO/PAT −0.0505x. Inventory absorbed ₹335.3193 crore, receivables ₹257.5198 crore, offset by payables ₹158.3512 and other-liability ₹289.9218 crore inflows. Other-current-liabilities include customer advances ₹148.7757 and other payables ₹346.0645 crore. Management attributes the latter category’s sharp growth to TReDS funding for suppliers; exact facility-level reconciliation was not disclosed. Reclassifying the ₹346.0633 crore increase as financing gives diagnostic CFO −₹221.4975 crore before cash interest, rather than asserting that the audited classification is invalid. Cash capex ₹41.4319 crore leaves reported FCF ₹83.1339 crore; cash finance/lease interest ₹40.7331 and lease principal ₹3.075 reduce that to ₹39.3258 crore before supplier-finance adjustment. Do not call reported CFO cash available to equity.

Receivables ₹791.9121 crore, inventory ₹536.3405 crore (WIP ₹475.9023), supplier advances ₹75.469 crore and tax/government balances ₹71.2823 crore expose collection/completion risk. Note 13 headline gross ₹794.9228 less ECL ₹3.0108 reconciles net ₹791.9120 approximately. The separate ageing table prints ₹788.9013 subtotal and then ₹791.9121 net despite an ECL deduction; the ₹6.0215 crore gross-table discrepancy is real in the visually checked source, not silently corrected. The table shows ₹57.6426 crore older than one year, subject to this reconciliation. No subsequent cash recovery is assumed.

Ind AS bridge FY25 PAT ₹115.3677+reclassification ₹0.5414−adjustment ₹2.7380=₹113.1711 crore versus rounded published ₹113.1713; lease/ECL/tax/gratuity adjustments are explained in transition notes. Older CFO is kept separate: FY24 original ₹54.0292 versus FY25 comparative ₹40.6146; FY25 original −₹158.0465 versus Ind AS −₹140.9309. General regrouping and “no material impact” language do not supply a complete cash-line bridge. Both FY25 versions nevertheless establish severe cash weakness. Original FY23 CFO −₹32.3768 crore is not replaced by a differently scoped prospectus snippet.

Equity+debt+leases−cash capital is ₹653.5082 crore FY25. Including ₹346.0645 crore supplier-finance proxy, FY26 capital ₹1,204.2457 crore. Normalized 25%-tax NOPAT ₹237.8263/123.1355 gives 25.60% average-capital and 20.82% incremental return. These include CWIP and funding rather than excluding immature assets. Other bank balances ₹176.2326 crore are not netted as free cash; reported cash-equivalent ₹166.757 crore is. Capital returns remain historical proxies, not proven returns on Onix/BESS. [S1][S3][S4][S5]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Dated 19 October secondary close ₹290.60 times 111,671,485 shares implies ₹3,245.1734 crore market capitalization, approximately 15.95× FY26 owners’ PAT and 14.88× TTM owners’ PAT. Those multiples do not fund the project pipeline. The attached five-year model separates core EPC/manufacturing/service cash flow from three project schedules, subtracts project equity calls, charges opening debt plus half-year new-draw interest, includes construction interest in sponsor funding, and deducts project debt before ownership allocation. Opening economic debt ₹638.4791 crore includes financial debt, leases and the full supplier-finance sensitivity; operating NWC ₹849.9716 crore excludes that financing liability to avoid double counting. All ₹176.2326 crore other-bank balances are withheld from surplus cash.

Bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹28.97/658.17/1455.05 imply −36.94%/+17.76%/+38.01% annually, before transaction costs and taxes, with no distributions. Base requires ₹685.91 crore additional core borrowing and ₹665.57 crore listed-share project equity calls; peak core economic debt ₹1,324.39 crore excludes project borrowing. These are conditional requirements, not available sanctioned headroom. Full new-debt facilities, nonfund guarantees and proposed credit cannot be added together as cash. Core terminal multiples 8/11/14× EBIT and project EBITDA multiples are assumptions, with two-way margin/multiple and 15/18/21%DCF sensitivities. The core NCI haircut 3.6% is a simplifying historical profit-share proxy, not a legal ownership waterfall. Onix 60% is verified; model TN/AP 100% attribution is an explicit unverified simplifying assumption.

IPO-era warrants were fully converted in May 2025; no additional warrant cash is counted. April 2026 allotment 78,000 shares at ₹2 raises issued 111,671,485. Remaining 78,000 options are conservatively exercised, giving 111,749,485 modeled shares and ₹0.0156 crore cash, not millions of new funding. Historical stock split is outside the July–October liquidity window. 60/60 secondary rows exist; low×volume mean/median ₹42.1437/32.7478 million and 20-day ₹50.8295/34.9427 million give conditional ₹5 lakh exits 0.763/0.305/0.153 days at 2/5/10% 60-day participation. These are proxy bounds, not actual BSE turnover or guaranteed fills. Lot 200 costs ₹58,120; eight lots ₹464,960 approximate the reference. No primary BSE restriction/depth clearance is inferred from the active master. [S1][S6][S7][S10][S13][S95] [S91]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A 30-day receivable extension on FY26 sales requires ₹233.6552 crore, a 10% inventory haircut ₹53.6341 crore and a 10% guarantee crystallization ₹51.6118 crore before recovery. Treat these as distinct conditional shocks, not a simultaneous forecast or automatic loss. Supplier finance could refinance or reverse rather than remain permanent interest-free capital. Bear project equity calls ₹1,186.01 crore and core borrowing ₹1,730.84 crore expose rescue-financing dependence; the positive calculated terminal price is not a downside floor. Funding failure, contractual step-in rights or forced issuance can produce worse equity outcomes, including total loss. Base plus ₹250 crore additional land/equity commitment increases modeled core debt peak to ₹1,604.37 crore and lowers return to 16.67%, before any further project revenue, demonstrating the cost of an unfunded pipeline. [S1][S5]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold appreciation requires 37.97%/58.49% annual returns. At ₹290.60 and 111,749,485 diluted shares, a 5× price at 15× exit P/E requires approximately ₹1,082.48 crore owners’ PAT; 10× requires ₹2,164.96 crore, versus FY26 ₹203.48 crore. At 7% net owners’ margin,5× requires roughly ₹15,464 crore sales, before financing dilution and project minority claims. The bull diagnostic reaches about 5× only with large core growth, sustained 11.5% EBIT margin, faster working-capital turnover, funded projects and 14× exit multiple together. Its 38.01% return is not a verified probability or base case. A 20% new equity issuance without incremental value reduces per-share terminal values 16.67%; a fully funded issuance requires separate cash/proceeds use, not this simple dilution stress. [S1][S10][S95]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Each result: reconcile collections and ageing-table totals; inventory WIP billing/completion; TReDS balances, recourse, rates and bank classification; cash versus lien deposits; actual customer advances and related-party EPC eliminations. Each project: obtain signed capex budget, amount already spent, equity waterfall, debt disbursement and amortization, recourse/guarantees, tariff/availability penalties, VGF receipt and battery replacement reserve. Track commissioning against independently acknowledged offtake milestones, not only management MW claims. Verify any effective migration date and lot change from exchange notices; recheck BSE restrictions and executable depth before sizing. Review immediately after equity issuance, large guarantee draw, project delay or lender covenant event. [S1][S2][S5][S6][S7][S11][S12]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved forward funding and project economics. Historical operating quality can be ranked with medium confidence; IAS cannot because the calculated return depends on financing/ownership/timing assumptions whose exact terms are unavailable. This is not a presumption of insolvency, misconduct or an automatic rejection of reported growth. A full project funding/recourse bridge, independently supported collection evidence and executable market assessment could convert the diagnostic into an investment valuation. Migration approval alone cannot do so.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Three annual reports, current quarter, primary acquisition/loan/order/ESOP filings, earnings calls and recent commissioning updates were reviewed. Earlier issuer-hosted prospectus/FY23 links redirected to the new site or failed; the available FY24 comparative supplies FY23 history, not an invented five-year series. Revised June results were located and screened but scanned half-year formatting was not used to overwrite signed annual statements. The exact old-to-new CFO bridge and ageing subtotal remain unresolved after primary cross-checks. Full model schedules are completed, but TN/AP ownership, remaining cost/disbursement split, project interest/amortization and supplier-finance mapping remain explicit assumptions. Whole project budgets are charged forward without credit for unverified prior project spend, a conservative overstatement risk; unknown existing project debt in group balances can also overlap the core proxy. No claim of precise October net debt or fully committed model funding. Peer sources establish business-model fit only, not current peer valuation. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S9][S11][S12][S13]
